correctness.rationale: For \(0<\alpha<1\), Bernstein subordination makes every fractional off-diagonal strictly negative and rows sum to zero, giving the exact endpoint norm 2 max diagonal. Reflection of the cosine path eigenspace onto the doubled cycle and strict beta-integral monotonicity place the unique (odd) or paired (even) central maxima. Gamma-ratio asymptotics, uniform summability of image tails and a paired even-path expansion yield the stated zeta/parity coefficient with the correct \(O_\alpha(n^{-5-2\alpha})\) remainder; a separate alpha-uniform \(O(\kappa_\alpha n^{-3-2\alpha})\) estimate yields the logarithmic crossover. A reproducible independent numerical formulation ran 2775 finite assertions; finite checks are supportive rather than universal proof.

value.rationale: The exact endpoint norm is an intrinsically motivated worst-case stability invariant of a finite reflecting fractional diffusion generator. The strict central maximizers are nontrivial global localization statements. The two-term finite-size coefficient detects the difference between odd and even paths invisible to their common leading asymptotic, and the \(\alpha\asymp 1/\log n\) double limit resolves a noncommuting zero-order finite/infinite-volume transition. These facts classify all n and the full interval \(0<\alpha<1\), not an arbitrary small instance or a routine parameter substitution.
